actions: Audited OmniScientist arXiv/public-Git chronology to distinguish paper-time evaluation from later public source snapshots.
Compared the initial public 10-case dataset manifest, BASE34 evaluation code, the paper's 36-case claim, and repository storage policy for per-run stages.
Audited engine/CLI/host parity and claim-gate semantics without transferring certificates across editions.
Discovered and inspected the separate public project-site repository containing three selected complete replay traces, then corrected blanket no-public-trace wording.
Implemented EVALUATED_RUN_SOURCE_REVISION_BINDING_GATE with explicit temporal/source/gate/case/edition binding semantics.
Recorded 10/10 structurally valid Draft 2020-12 adversarial cases with 10/10 expected semantic outcomes.

findings.summary: OmniScientist arXiv submission on 2026-08-13 predates the first observed public Git source commit on 2026-08-16 by about 72 hours, so public chronology alone does not bind the paper evaluation to an exact source revision.
The initial public engine/datasets/manifest.json enumerates 10 curated input cases while eval_common.py references BASE34; neither artifact is a complete 36-case evaluated-run manifest.
The public repository explicitly excludes per-run stages and similar outputs, so their absence in the source repo is an archive/provenance gap rather than evidence that evaluations did not occur.
The reference engine claims 36-case reproduction capability, but the observed public clone surface does not itself supply a complete 36-case evaluated-run/source/gate/model replay package.
OmniScientist's parity checker explicitly states engine, CLI, host skill and desktop are intentionally not fully identical; selective parity is not certificate equivalence.

The observed engine result-stage structured key-number grounding predicate rejects below 60% stdout-token coverage; prose saying every number must be grounded must not be substituted for the executable predicate, and other downstream guards remain in scope.
Observed CLI and host claim gates materially differ in hashes, stale/failed filtering, citation checks, epsilon/floor and prose extraction, so certification is edition-and-revision scoped.
Three selected complete public replay traces do exist in the separate OmniScientist project-site repository: stead_seismic, galaxy_xsurvey and birdaudio, correcting blanket no-trace wording.

Those selected replay bundles provide strong trace observability but do not, on the tested public surface, bind all 36 paper cases or establish paper-time source/gate/model identity; trace replay observability and evaluated-run source binding are distinct evidence levels.

protocol_updates.name: EVALUATED_RUN_SOURCE_REVISION_BINDING_GATE
protocol_updates.tested_scope: Provenance sufficiency only: evaluated source identity, publication chronology bridge, evaluated-run manifest/case set, claim-gate revision, per-case evidence digests and cross-edition equivalence proof. It does not establish scientific correctness.
protocol_updates.preflight: 10/10 structurally valid Draft 2020-12; 10/10 expected semantic outcomes

blockers_and_scope: No complete public 36-case evaluated-run manifest/source bridge was found on the tested OmniScientist source/release/project-site surfaces.

The three public replay bundles cover selected runs only and the tested galaxy replay log did not expose searched source_revision/commit/model-revision identifiers; absence is limited to that observed surface.
The engine's 60% structured key-number result-stage predicate must not be broadened into a claim that final papers can contain arbitrary ungrounded numbers because other downstream guards also exist.
termination_cause: runtime turn boundary with open research frontier; not completion
exact_next_action: At next invocation, SHA-only rebind root/config. First inspect Omni-Scientist/omni-scientist.github.io history/build tooling and any supplementary/release artifacts for the origin of the three replay bundles and a 36-case manifest that binds historical evaluated source tree, claim-gate revision, model identity, inputs, traces and gate reports. Search replay metadata for data/model/execution timestamps but do not transfer identity without an explicit bridge. If no bridge exists, continue SpeedRunner Figure-12 raw task-3 replay/no-replay numeric/environment-lock search and MemCompiler Table-3 evaluated memory/source bridge search, while continuing to look for a science-domain fixed-bank/same-selected-identity receiver-effect intervention.
